papers.title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
papers.problem: Teams cannot compare privacy tests for split language models, because each test uses different attacker access, data, and scoring.
papers.fix: Added training gradients raised token recovery from 94.20% to 97.38% and whole-document recovery from 13.71% to 37.77%.
papers.practicalUseCase: Attacker access changes privacy results a lot, so state the attacker, data, and scoring rule in every privacy claim.
papers.limitation: The shown result comes from one controlled GPT-2 experiment, so other models may behave differently.

papers.title: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Build Their Own Feedback for Recursive Self-Improvement?
papers.problem: Running full AI benchmarks again and again costs too much, and cheaper agent-built tests were untested.
papers.fix: AI-built test suites ranked about 75% of model pairs the same way as real benchmarks, against a 91% ceiling.
papers.practicalUseCase: A cheap AI-built test can guide quick model checks, but a human-picked sample of public tasks still works well.
papers.limitation: Agent-built tests still cut off answers, run out of budget, or let a few questions dominate a score.

papers.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages
papers.problem: Diffusion language models spend very different amounts of work on outputs of the same length, and the cause was unclear.
papers.fix: Story writing needs over three times more passes per token than grammar fixes; speed-weighted answers beat voting by 4.2 points.
papers.practicalUseCase: Expect cheap runs on copy-and-edit jobs, costly runs on open writing, and treat slow decoding as a warning.
papers.limitation: The study covers only two diffusion models across 10 tasks.

papers.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
papers.problem: Compressing diffusion language models hurts accuracy, because each task needs different precision at different denoising steps.
papers.fix: T2Quant sets precision per step without labels and lifted accuracy by up to 6.7 points at equal budget.
papers.practicalUseCase: Match compression precision to the task and the step to keep accuracy while you shrink the model.
papers.limitation: Tests covered three diffusion models and six benchmarks, so other models may not gain as much.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but it was unclear whether they lead to real environmental action.
papers.fix: Committees raised environmental scores in emerging-market banks, but in Islamic banks they lifted only overall scores and resource reduction.
papers.practicalUseCase: A committee alone may give Islamic banks only symbolic gains, so check for real green products and innovations.
papers.limitation: The study uses panel regressions on banks in emerging markets, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Little was known about how sustainability sukuk grew or what decides the size of each issue.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issues, sustainability sukuk stayed tiny, and equity-based contracts gave larger issues than sale-based ones.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers should pick equity-based contracts, and policymakers should offer incentives, because second party opinion costs shrink issue size.
papers.limitation: The data stops at 2022 and shows links between features and issue size, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan did not know whether AI and big data actually improve competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.fix: AI, big data analytics, and data management all raised competitiveness and sustainable development; staff digital skill raised only competitiveness.
papers.practicalUseCase: Invest in AI, analytics, and data management first, because staff digital skill alone will not lift sustainable development.
papers.limitation: The survey covers 214 managers at 15 Jordanian Islamic banks at one time, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks in dual banking systems lacked clear evidence on what drives their expansion.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries, ICT adoption drove expansion most, and high-tech exports helped only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks should invest in digital tools first, because high-tech exports alone give no clear growth gain.
papers.limitation: The sample covers 12 countries and 2010 to 2023 only, so other markets may differ.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many people in Muslim-majority countries still lack formal financial services, even as Islamic finance grew.
papers.fix: In 35 countries, OIC financial inclusion depends on income, schooling, institutions, internet access, population, and age dependency.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC countries need more digital infrastructure, youth and women empowerment, and higher income to widen financial inclusion.
papers.limitation: The study covers 35 countries from 2005 to 2021 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant tests and comparison, and no one knew how often they feel like impostors.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were frequent among medical students worldwide, though results varied a lot by sampling method and region.
papers.practicalUseCase: If impostor feelings are common, schools should measure them one standard way and test help for coping and training culture.
papers.limitation: Results differed widely between studies, so the pooled estimate needs careful reading.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Generative AI helps doctoral students, but it was unclear what makes them truly innovative with it.
papers.fix: Both inner and outer motivation drive innovation together, and strong AI literacy makes motivation turn into innovation more efficiently.
papers.practicalUseCase: Build AI literacy and good research support, because they help innovation even when motivation is low.
papers.limitation: The study uses one self-reported survey in chemistry, so it cannot prove cause and may show bias.
